Hi Mina / Olga,

Thanks for taking a look. Please find attached our DPA redline (Medisphere_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf) and a short security questionnaire. Two clauses we flagged as potentially blocking for Medisphere go live:

1) Section 4.2 (Telemetry & Quality Monitoring): Medisphere wants a carveout that allows persistent request-level telemetry (including hashed IDs and request/response metadata) to be exported to our analytics vendor for monitoring product quality and safety. They are asking for a 90-day retention window by default.

2) Section 7.1 (No Personalization / Model Training): They want explicit language permitting non-personal "behavioral telemetry" to be used for improving ML models that do not include any PII or content used for training individualized models for Medisphere customers.

These are material asks for us; they indicated timeline pressure for an onboarding by Oct 14. Can Redwood Product & Security confirm impact to runtime and whether the requested carveout is acceptable with compensating controls?

Also included: DocuSign link stub (DocuSign_Link.txt). Procurement (Ben) is on copy to coordinate billing/account setup.

Best,

Mina — quick thoughts from Security (high level):

We can probably accept telemetry exports that contain pseudonymized/hashes IDs provided the following controls are in place:
- Hashing must be one-way with per-customer salt managed by Redwood KMS (no reversible mapping stored).
- Export must be scoped to aggregated/streamed telemetry only; no raw request payload or full response text allowed.
- Retention cap: recommend 30 days default; 90 days is higher risk. If business requires 90d, we need a documented risk acceptance + reviewed vendor security profile and SOC2 Type II (within last 12 months).
- Vendor contract: Medisphere must include Vendor Appendix naming the analytics vendor; we must reserve right to refuse vendor on security grounds.
- Auditability: export requests must be logged and surfaced in Console (route, model, consumer).

Practical runtime implications: we do not currently support customer-scoped salted hashing at export time for hosted customers — it's implementable but will require (a) a small runtime change to apply per-customer salt during export, (b) a limited config surface in Console, and (c) an ops playbook for vetting vendors. Rough estimate: 2 engineering sprints to have a hardened export path + 1 security review. If Product prefers, we can offer a stopgap: allow exports through our existing telemetry service with manual vetting and a signed vendors appendix — higher operational overhead for us.

I'll also need the completed security questionnaire and vendor SOC2 link.

- Olga
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — product perspective: we understand why Medisphere wants the telemetry for QA/clinical safety monitoring. A few notes on scope and roadmap impact:

1) "Non-personalization" is acceptable only if we can guarantee that the exported telemetry cannot be re-associated to an identifiable user or used to train customer-targeted models. We should require: hashed ID with per-customer salt (as Olga suggested), no raw response payload, and a bounded retention.

2) Runtime work: the follow-up engineering items Olga mentioned are real. I validated with Infra: implementing per-customer salts in the export pipeline and a toggle in Console is ~2 sprints (5-person team) to reach a stable rollout (including e2e tests); add 1 sprint for docs and playbook. If we need 90-day retention as a hard requirement, storage/costs and legal/ops coordination increases — estimate +0.5 sprint ongoing cost.

3) Proposed product compromise (fast path):
- Phase 0 (manual): Accept Medisphere export via a manual, reviewed export flow (ops-run, vet vendor, short-term white-list) — can be done immediately but with a one-off service charge.
- Phase 1 (platform): Build per-customer-salt export path + Console toggle; target delivery: 8 weeks.

I've opened INF-4321 to track the work and linked the security questionnaire. If Legal can draft a tight clause restricting downstream vendor usage and prohibiting training on any customer content, Product can support the Phase 0 + Phase 1 flow.

Karthik
Director, Product — Platform

Thanks all — contracting suggestions from my side:

- Accept telemetry export under the following redlined language (draft):
"Provider may export aggregated and pseudonymized telemetry data necessary for Customer's quality and safety monitoring. Pseudonymization shall use a one-way hash with a per-customer secret managed by Provider; exported telemetry shall not include full request or response content, direct identifiers, or any data intended for training individualized models. Retention of exported telemetry shall not exceed 30 days unless mutually agreed in writing with documented security justification and Vendor Appendix listing analytics vendor(s)."

- This preserves Product's and Security's constraints, keeps training risk limited, and gives Medisphere a clear path to request longer retention with documented justification.

- For Phase 0 (manual export), add a clause: "Provider may, as a one-off operational accommodation, allow exports under a manual review and Vendor Appendix; such accommodations may be subject to additional fees and must be renewed every 12 months."

Laura / Ben — if Medisphere can accept the 30-day default and complete the questionnaire + provide SOC2 for the vendor, Legal is comfortable pushing this through as the initial contract position. If they insist on 90d unconditional retention, we need an executive level exception.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
